note: SAS advisory implementation guidance for a provider hosted on Microsoft Azure (story MCE-17). Identification only: each service is named so a provider can locate the vendor's own documentation; nothing here evaluates any product or makes any FedRAMP determination about it, and the rule or KSI statement governs. Service names and documentation URLs were captured from the vendor's public documentation on the capture date; the notes are not vendor text. Deleting this file withdraws the platform (THIRD_PARTY_NOTICE.md, section Removing a third party).

family_guidance.CMU: Use FIPS 140 validated cryptographic modules for federal data: Azure Key Vault Managed HSM or hardware-protected keys in Azure Key Vault, and TLS 1.2 or higher. Record module certificates and validation numbers; document any exception formally.
family_guidance.IEC: Define incident evaluation and reporting procedures with the FedRAMP Reportable Incident test, the Potential Agency Impact N-rating scale, and the class-specific reporting timeframes. Wire detection (Microsoft Sentinel incidents, Microsoft Defender for Cloud alerts) to an on-call process that can meet the clock.
family_guidance.MAS: Define the Minimum Assessment Scope narrowly and defensibly: identify every information resource that handles federal data or whose compromise would affect it, justify each exclusion, and keep the inventory machine-generated (Azure Resource Graph exports) so it stays current.
family_guidance.VDR: Run continuous vulnerability detection across every in-scope resource (Microsoft Defender for Cloud vulnerability assessment for virtual machines and container images, Azure Update Manager patch status), meet the class cadences for sample and drift detection, track mitigation and remediation against the timeframes, and honor CISA KEV due dates.

ksi_guidance.KSI-CED-RAT: Review all training content and completion on a defined cycle; keep the review dated and owned. Where completion records live in a learning system, export them on the same cycle. Evidence: review records with reviewer, date and outcome, plus the updated training register.
ksi_guidance.KSI-CMT-LMC: Log and monitor every modification to the offering: the Azure Monitor Activity Log exported to a Log Analytics workspace in a separate subscription, resource change history through Azure Resource Graph, Azure Monitor alert rules on writes made outside the pipeline's identity. Evidence: diagnostic settings exports, change history queries, alert history.
ksi_guidance.KSI-CMT-RMV: Deploy changes by redeploying version-controlled resources (Bicep templates through Azure Pipelines), not by editing live resources. Evidence: pipeline deployment records diffed against Activity Log write operations; what-if and drift results.
ksi_guidance.KSI-CMT-RVP: Review change management procedure effectiveness on a cycle: measure failed changes, rollbacks and out-of-band changes, and adjust the procedure. Evidence: dated reviews with metrics and resulting changes.
ksi_guidance.KSI-CMT-VTD: Automate testing and validation of changes in Azure Pipelines: pre-deployment tests, Azure Policy evaluation of templates before deployment, Microsoft Defender for Cloud DevOps security scanning, post-deployment verification. Evidence: pipeline run records showing each gate passed per change.
ksi_guidance.KSI-CNA-DFP: Strictly define functionality and privileges for infrastructure and services: least-privilege role assignments scoped through Azure management groups, Azure Policy deny effects, Microsoft Entra ID Governance access packages. Evidence: role assignment exports, policy assignment inventory, unused-permission review records.
ksi_guidance.KSI-CNA-EIS: Class-varying (optional/MAY at Class B, required at Class C): automated services persistently assess the security of all machine-based information resources and automatically enforce their intended operational state. On Microsoft Azure: Azure Policy with deployIfNotExists and modify effects plus remediation tasks, Azure Machine Configuration for in-guest settings. Evidence: policy compliance state history, remediation task records, machine configuration reports over time.
ksi_guidance.KSI-CNA-IBP: Persistently check third-party machine-based resources against the original provider's documented secure-configuration benchmarks: Microsoft Defender for Cloud regulatory compliance standards and secure score assessments, Azure Machine Configuration baselines. Evidence: assessment results per standard over time.
ksi_guidance.KSI-CNA-MAT: Minimize attack surface and lateral movement: Azure Private Link for platform services, network security groups that deny by default, Azure Policy that blocks public network access and public blob access. Evidence: policy compliance state for exposure rules, network design records, Microsoft Defender for Cloud exposure findings trend.
ksi_guidance.KSI-CNA-OFA: Review resources for high availability and rapid recovery: availability zone deployment, health probes on load balancers, Azure Site Recovery plans, tested recovery. Evidence: architecture inventory with zone coverage, recovery test records.
ksi_guidance.KSI-CNA-RNT: Limit inbound and outbound network traffic: network security groups and Azure Firewall rules that deny by default, egress filtering, Azure Web Application Firewall on public entry points. Evidence: rule exports, Azure Network Watcher flow analysis, firewall coverage inventory.
ksi_guidance.KSI-CNA-RVP: Review protection against denial of service and unwanted activity: Azure DDoS Protection on public virtual networks, Azure Web Application Firewall rate limiting, Microsoft Defender for Cloud alert review. Evidence: protection coverage inventory and dated effectiveness reviews.
ksi_guidance.KSI-CNA-ULN: Use logical networking to enforce traffic flow controls: virtual network segmentation, user-defined routes through Azure Firewall, Azure Private Link for service-to-service paths, Azure Network Watcher flow logs. Evidence: network architecture records, flow log analysis, connectivity troubleshooting results.
ksi_guidance.KSI-IAM-AAM: Automate the lifecycle and privileges of all accounts, roles and groups: Microsoft Entra ID with automated provisioning from the authoritative identity source, Microsoft Entra ID Governance lifecycle workflows and access reviews, automated deprovisioning on termination. Evidence: provisioning logs, access review records, orphan-account checks.
ksi_guidance.KSI-IAM-APM: Use passwordless authentication where feasible (FIDO2 security keys or passkeys), otherwise phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication enforced through Microsoft Entra Conditional Access; eliminate long-lived credentials. Evidence: authentication method policy exports, sign-in log analysis, credential inventory.
ksi_guidance.KSI-IAM-ELP: Ensure each user and device can only access what it needs: Microsoft Entra ID Governance access reviews, least-privilege role design, Microsoft Entra Conditional Access device requirements for administrative access. Evidence: access review records, unused-access findings and their closure.
ksi_guidance.KSI-IAM-JIT: Use a least-privileged, role-based, just-in-time authorization model: Privileged Identity Management eligible assignments activated with approval and expiry; no standing privileged assignments. Evidence: activation logs with approvals and automatic expiry.
ksi_guidance.KSI-IAM-SNU: Use appropriately secure authentication for non-user accounts and services: Microsoft Entra managed identities and workload identity federation; no long-lived client secrets; rotate any unavoidable secrets in Azure Key Vault. Evidence: credential inventory, secret-age reports, Azure Key Vault rotation status.
ksi_guidance.KSI-IAM-SUS: Disable or secure privileged accounts in response to suspicious activity: Microsoft Sentinel analytics rules and Microsoft Defender for Cloud alerts wired to automated response (disable accounts, revoke sessions) with on-call escalation. Evidence: response runbooks plus executed-response records with timestamps.
ksi_guidance.KSI-INR-AAR: Generate after action reports for incidents and incorporate lessons persistently. Evidence: after action reports linked to incidents, with tracked improvement actions and closure.
ksi_guidance.KSI-INR-RIR: Review incident response procedure effectiveness on a cycle, including exercises. Evidence: dated reviews, exercise records, and procedure updates that resulted.
ksi_guidance.KSI-INR-RPI: Review past incidents for patterns and previously missed vulnerabilities. Evidence: periodic pattern-analysis reports referencing the incident register.
ksi_guidance.KSI-MLA-ALA: Class-varying (optional/MAY at Class B, required at Class C): a least-privileged, role/attribute-based, just-in-time authorization model governs access to log data by data sensitivity, and is persistently reviewed. On Microsoft Azure: Log Analytics workspaces in a dedicated subscription, Privileged Identity Management for time-bound log access, table-level access control in Azure Monitor. Evidence: role assignments on the logging subscription, activation records, periodic access reviews of the log store.
ksi_guidance.KSI-MLA-EVC: Persistently evaluate and test the configuration of machine-based resources, especially infrastructure as code: policy-as-code in Azure Pipelines on Bicep templates, Azure Policy evaluation in runtime, Microsoft Defender for Cloud misconfiguration assessments. Evidence: pipeline policy results per change and compliance state over time.
ksi_guidance.KSI-MLA-LET: Maintain and review a list of resources and event types that will be logged, monitored and audited, and confirm those activities occur: the register mapped to Azure Monitor diagnostic settings per resource type. Evidence: the logging register plus diagnostic setting exports proving each listed source emits.
ksi_guidance.KSI-MLA-OSM: Operate a SIEM or similar for centralized, tamper-resistant logging: Microsoft Sentinel on a Log Analytics workspace in a separate subscription, long-term export to Azure Blob Storage with immutable storage policies, restricted access. Evidence: workspace and export configuration, immutability policy status, access policies.
ksi_guidance.KSI-MLA-RVL: Persistently review and audit logs: automated detections (Microsoft Sentinel analytics rules, Microsoft Defender for Cloud alerts, Azure Monitor alert rules) plus a documented human review cadence for what automation cannot judge. Evidence: detection inventory, alert dispositions, review records.
ksi_guidance.KSI-PIY-GIV: Generate real-time inventories automatically from authoritative sources: Azure Resource Graph queries as the inventory of record, exportable on demand. Evidence: on-demand inventory exports with timestamps proving real-time generation.
ksi_guidance.KSI-PIY-RES: Demonstrate and review executive support for security goals persistently: executive sponsorship in the charter, recurring leadership reviews of posture, funded remediation. Evidence: dated leadership review records and funding decisions tied to security goals.
ksi_guidance.KSI-PIY-RIS: Review the effectiveness of security investments persistently: track spend against measurable outcomes (findings closed, coverage gained) and adjust. Evidence: periodic investment-effectiveness reviews with metrics and resulting decisions.
ksi_guidance.KSI-PIY-RSD: Review the effectiveness of security and privacy in the SDLC against CISA Secure By Design principles: pipeline security gates, secure defaults, threat modeling. Evidence: SDLC review records mapped to Secure By Design principles with improvement actions.
ksi_guidance.KSI-PIY-RVD: Operate and persistently review a vulnerability disclosure program: a public intake channel, triage SLAs, and periodic effectiveness review. Evidence: the published policy, intake and triage records, dated program reviews.
ksi_guidance.KSI-SCR-MIT: Persistently identify, review, and mitigate supply chain risks: supplier vetting, dependency review, risk register entries with mitigations. Evidence: the supply chain risk register with review dates and mitigation status.
ksi_guidance.KSI-SCR-MON: Automatically monitor third-party software for upstream vulnerabilities: Microsoft Defender for Cloud container image scanning in Azure Container Registry, dependency scanning in Azure Pipelines, software bill of materials tracking, advisory feeds. Evidence: scan results over time, advisory response records, SBOM currency.
ksi_guidance.KSI-RPL-ABO: Keep backups aligned with defined recovery objectives: Azure Backup policies matching the stated recovery point objective, cross-region restore where the objectives require, Azure Site Recovery for replication. Evidence: backup policy configuration, job success history, restore points against objectives.
ksi_guidance.KSI-RPL-ARP: Maintain a recovery plan aligned with objectives, covering roles, procedures, and dependencies. Evidence: the plan with review dates and alignment to the stated RTO and RPO.
ksi_guidance.KSI-RPL-RRO: Define recovery time and recovery point objectives and keep them current. Evidence: documented RTO and RPO with rationale and review history.
ksi_guidance.KSI-RPL-TRC: Test the capability to recover from incidents and contingencies: restore tests from Azure Backup, Azure Site Recovery failover drills, Azure Chaos Studio experiments, measured against objectives. Evidence: test records with measured times against objectives and corrective actions.
ksi_guidance.KSI-SVC-ACM: Manage configuration with automation and review drift persistently: infrastructure as code as the source of truth (Bicep through Azure Pipelines), Azure Policy compliance state for drift, Azure Machine Configuration for in-guest drift, automated remediation where safe. Evidence: drift findings and their resolution over time.
ksi_guidance.KSI-SVC-ASM: Automate management, protection, and rotation of keys, certificates, and secrets: Azure Key Vault key rotation policies, certificate auto-renewal in Azure Key Vault, secret rotation through Azure Automation or event-driven functions. Evidence: rotation status across all three, alerts on failures.
ksi_guidance.KSI-SVC-EIS: Persistently evaluate resources for security improvement opportunities and implement them: Microsoft Defender for Cloud assessments and secure score triage with tracked adoption. Evidence: assessment trend plus a record of improvements shipped.
ksi_guidance.KSI-SVC-PRR: Class-varying (optional/MAY at Class B, required at Class C): plans, procedures, and resource state are persistently reviewed after changes to limit and remove unwanted residual elements that could affect confidentiality, integrity, or availability of federal customer data. On Microsoft Azure: post-change review of Azure Resource Graph change history for orphaned resources, cleanup through the pipeline. Evidence: post-change review records, residual-resource cleanup logs.
ksi_guidance.KSI-SVC-RUD: Class-varying (optional/MAY at Class B, required at Class C): unwanted federal customer data is removed promptly when an agency requests it per customer agreements, including from backups where appropriate (e.g. data spill or usage change). On Microsoft Azure: deletion procedures that cover Azure Blob Storage versions and soft-deleted data as well as Azure Backup recovery points. Evidence: data-removal request handling records, backup-scoped deletion procedures and logs.
ksi_guidance.KSI-SVC-SIN: Encrypt or otherwise secure information from unwanted access or modification: customer-managed keys in Azure Key Vault or Azure Key Vault Managed HSM, TLS 1.2 or higher in transit, Azure Policy that requires encryption settings and blocks public access. Evidence: policy compliance state for encryption rules, key usage records.
ksi_guidance.KSI-SVC-VCM: Class-varying (optional/MAY at Class B, required at Class C): the authenticity and integrity of communications between machine-based information resources is persistently validated using automation. On Microsoft Azure: mutual TLS between services, Microsoft Entra managed identities for service-to-service authentication, signed inter-service requests. Evidence: identity validation records, automated integrity-verification records.
ksi_guidance.KSI-SVC-VRI: Use cryptographic methods to validate the integrity of machine-based resources: signed container images in Azure Container Registry with digests pinned in deployment, Azure Attestation for platform integrity where used, signed pipeline artifacts. Evidence: signature or digest verification records in the pipeline, attestation reports.
